label: lmm:vershynin
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lmm:vershynin}
    Let $N\in {\mathbb N}^*$. There exists an absolute constant $C$ that does not depend on $N$ such that the event $E^N \subset \Omega$ defined by 

    $$E^N= \left \{\left \|\Xi-{\mathbf E} \left[\Xi\right] \right \|_2 \leq C \sqrt N \right \}$$
     has a probability ${\mathbf P}$ larger than $1-2\mathrm e^{-N}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This Lemma is a direct application of Theorem 4.4.5 in \cite{vershynin}. Indeed, the entries of our matrix are independent and of zero mean. Moreover, since we have in total $q \times q$ centered Bernoulli distributions, the maximum Sub-Gaussian norm $\max_{(i,j) \in \{1,\cdots,N\}^2}\|\left(\Xi-{\mathbf E} \left[\Xi\right]\right)^{ij}\|_{\psi^2}$ is bounded by a quantity that does not depend on $N$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: If the kernel $\phi$ as well as the baseline pre-intensities $\mu$ are non-negative, then the jump rate can be chosen $\psi(x)=x$. This particular choice yields the linear Poisson autoregression, which does not allow for inhibition. However, it allows us to have explicit recursive formulae for ${\mathbb E} \left[Y_t\right]$ as well as to perform the likelihood approximation studied in Section \ref{sec:application}.
head: environment

label: ass:stability_MF
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:stability_MF}
    If $\bar M \in \mathcal M_q({\mathbb R}_+)$ denotes the matrix 
    $$\bar M_{h\ell}=L\alpha_\ell p_{\ell \to h} \mathcal S \left(\left |\phi^{\ell \to h} \right |\right),$$
    then $\bar M$ has a spectral radius strictly less than one ($\rho(\bar M)<1$).
head: environment

label: prop:cvg_bar_k
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:cvg_bar_k}
    If Assumption \ref{ass:stability_MF} holds, then the equation
    $$\lambda_\infty^h=\psi \left(\mu_h + \sum_{\ell=1}^q \alpha_\ell p_{\ell \to h} \mathcal S\left(\phi^{\ell \to h}\right) \lambda_\infty^\ell \right ),\quad h\in \{1,\cdots,q\}$$
    has a unique solution in $ {\mathbb R}_+^q$. Moreover, the sequence $(\bar\lambda_t)_{t\in {\mathbb N}}$ defined recursively in Equation \eqref{def: lambda_bar} converges to $\lambda_\infty$ as $t\to +\infty$.

title: Proof
body_md: The proof of this Proposition can be found in Section \ref{proof: cvg_bar_k}.

label: lemma:hat_lambda
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma:hat_lambda}
   Let $N$ be a fixed number of nodes in ${\mathbb N}^*$ and $T  \in {\mathbb N}^*$ be the time horizon. If Assumption \ref{ass: crucial} holds, then, there exist two positive constants $C$ and $c$ that do not depend on $N$ nor $T$ such that on the event $E^N$ (such that ${\mathbf P} (E^N) \ge 1-2\mathrm{e}^{-N}$) we have that 
    $$\left \|\hat \lambda ^{N}_{t}\right\|_2 \leq C \sqrt{N} \exp\left( c\frac{T}{\sqrt N}\right)$$
    for all $t=1,\cdots,T$.                                                                                                
                                                                 
       If Assumption \ref{ass:crucial_strong} holds, then there exists a threshold $N_0$ that does not depend on time such that for any $N\ge N_0$
    $$\left \|\hat \lambda_t^{N} \right \|_2 \le C \sqrt N,$$
    for all $t \in {\mathbb N}$ on $E^N$.

title: Proof
body_md: The proof of this Lemma can be found in Section \ref{proof: hat_lambda}.

label: thm:main_l_2
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:main_l_2}
    Let $N$ be a fixed number of nodes in ${\mathbb N}^*$ and $T  \in {\mathbb N}^*$ be the time horizon. We recall that $\bar Y^{N}$ is defined in \eqref{def: Y_bar}. If Assumption \ref{ass: crucial} holds, then, there exist two positive constants $C$ and $c$ that do not depend on $N$ nor $T$ such that on the event $E^N$ (such that ${\mathbf P} (E^N) \ge 1-2\mathrm{e}^{-N}$) we have that 
    $$\frac{1}{N}\sum _{i=1}^N {\mathbb E} \left[ \left| Y_t^{i,N}-\bar Y^{i,N}_t\right|\right]\leq \frac{CT}{\sqrt N} \exp \left ( c\frac{T}{\sqrt N}\right),$$
    for all $t=1,\cdots,T$.                                                                                                
                                                                                                                 
     If instead of taking the uniform error in time and we bound the time average, we have that
     $$\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t=1}^T\frac{1}{N}\sum _{i=1}^N {\mathbb E} \left[ \left| Y_t^{i,N}-\bar Y^{i,N}_t\right|\right]\leq \frac{C}{\sqrt N} \exp \left ( c\frac{T}{\sqrt N}\right).$$
       If Assumption \ref{ass:crucial_strong} holds, then there exists a threshold $N_0$ that does not depend on time such that for any $N\ge N_0$
       $$\frac{1}{N}\sum _{i=1}^N {\mathbb E} \left[ \left| Y_t^{i,N}-\bar Y^{i,N}_t\right|\right]\leq \frac{C}{\sqrt N} ,$$
       for all $t \in {\mathbb N}$ on $E^N$.

$$\left \| {\mathbb E} \left [ \left| \lambda^{N}_{t+1}-\bar \lambda^{N}_{t+1}\right |\right]\right \|_\infty \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt {N^{1-2\varepsilon}}},$$
for all $t \in {\mathbb N}$ on $F^N \cap E^N$.

label: lmm:convolution
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Under a compact form, Inequality \eqref{ineq:conv} writes 
    $$|x_t| \preceq \left(A*|x|\right)_t+ W_t.$$
    By taking the convolution on the right and the left with $A^{(*m)}$ for some $m \in {\mathbb N}$ we have that 
    $$\left(A^{(*m)}*|x|\right)_t \preceq \left(A^{(*(m+1))}*|x|\right)_t+ \left(A^{(*m)}*W\right)_t,$$
    where the order has been preserved because taking the convolution involves adding and multiplying by positive matrices. Taking the telescopic sum of the last inequality yields 
$$|x_t|-\left(A^{(*(r+1))}*|x|\right)_t \preceq \left(\sum_{m=0}^{r}A^{(*m)}*W\right)_t,$$
for any $r \in {\mathbb N}$. For any $t \in {\mathbb N}$, we have that 
\begin{align*}
    \sum_{k=0}^t \left(A^{(*(r+1))}*|x|\right)_k &=\sum_{k=0}^t \sum_{j=0}^kA^{(*(r+1))}_j|x|_{k-j}\\
    &\preceq \left(\sum_{j=0}^{+\infty}A^{(*(r+1))}_j \right) \left(\sum_{k=0}^t|x|_k\right)\\
    &\preceq \left(\sum_{j=0}^{+\infty}A_j\right)^{r+1}\left(\sum_{k=0}^t|x|_k\right),
\end{align*}
and since $\rho \left(\sum_{j=0}^{+\infty}A_j\right)<1$, the right hand side of the last inequality converges to zero as $r$ grows to infinity, hence the result.
head: environment

label: lmm: euclidean_norm
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lmm: euclidean_norm}
    Let $\Phi^N$ be the kernel random matrix defined in Equation \eqref{def: Phi}. If Assumption \ref{ass: crucial} is in force, then we have that 
    $$\left \|\mathcal S\left({\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N\right]\right) \right\|_2 <1.$$
    And if Assumption \ref{ass:crucial_strong} holds, then 
    $$\mathcal S\left(\left \| {\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N\right] \right\|_2\right) <1.$$
    Similarly, if Assumption \ref{ass:uniform} holds, then
    $$\left \|\mathcal S\left({\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N\right]\right) \right\|_\infty <1,$$
    and if Assumption \ref{ass:uniform_strong} holds then,
    $$\mathcal S\left(\left \| {\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N\right] \right\|_\infty\right) <1.$$
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First, we have that 
    $$\mathcal S\left({\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N\right]\right)^{ij}=\frac 1 N Lp^{C(j)\to C(i)}\mathcal S \left(\left|\phi^{C(j) \to C(i)} \right |\right) .$$
    By introducing the rectangular matrix $\Theta \in \mathcal M_{N\times q} ({\mathbb R})$ defined by $\Theta_{ih}=\mathds 1 _{C(i)=h}$ and the square matrix $M' \in \mathcal M _{q \times q} ({\mathbb R})$ given by $M'_{h\ell}=p^{\ell \to h} \mathcal S \left(\left |\phi^{\ell \to h}\right |\right)$, we clearly have that 
    $$\mathcal S\left({\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N\right]\right) = \frac 1 N L \Theta M' \Theta ^\top .$$
    Using the sub-multiplicativity of the Euclidean norm and the fact that $\|\Theta \|_2=\sqrt {\rho \left(\Theta^\top \Theta\right)}=\sqrt {N \max_{h \in \{1,\cdots,q\}} \alpha_h}$ we have that  
    $$\left \| \mathcal S\left({\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N\right]\right)\right \|_2 \leq L \max_{h \in \{1,\cdots,q\}} \alpha_h \|M'\|_2$$
    and we conclude regarding the first point using Assumption \ref{ass: crucial}.\\
    For the second point we simply have that 
    \begin{align*}
        \left \| \mathcal S\left({\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N\right]\right)\right \|_\infty =& L \max_{1 \leq i \le N}\sum_{j=1}^N\frac 1 N p^{C(j)\to C(i)} \mathcal S \left( \left| \phi^{C(j)\to C(i)}\right |\right)\\
        =& L \max_{1 \leq h \le q}\sum_{\ell=1}^q \frac 1 N\sum_{j:C(j)=\ell} p^{\ell\to h} \mathcal S \left( \left| \phi^{\ell \to h}\right |\right)\\
         =& L \max_{1 \leq h \le q}\sum_{\ell=1}^q \alpha^\ell  p^{\ell\to h} \mathcal S \left( \left| \phi^{\ell \to h}\right |\right),
    \end{align*}
    which yields the result.
head: environment

label: lmm:average_adjacency
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lmm:average_adjacency}
    Let $N, T \in {\mathbb N}^*$ be two fixed integers. We recall that for $t=1,\cdots,T$ the random matrix $\Phi^N_t$ is given in Equation \eqref{def: Phi} by
    $$\left(\Phi^{ij,N}_{t}\right)=\frac{1}{N}L \xi_{j \to i} \phi ^{C(j)\to C(i)}_t.$$
    There exist then a positive constant $C$ that does not depend on $T$ nor on $N$ such that on the event $E^N$ (${\mathbf P}(E^N) \ge 1-2\mathrm e^{-N}$) we have 
    $$\left \|\Phi^N_t-{\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N_t\right]\right \|_2\leq C \sum_{h,\ell=1}^q \left |\phi^{h \to \ell}_t \right |\frac{1}{\sqrt N}$$
    for all $t \in \{1,\cdots,T\}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We recall that $\Xi=\left(\xi_{j \to i}\right)_{i,j=1,\cdots,N}$ is the adjacency matrix and we let $A_t$ be the $q \times q$ matrix defined by
    $$\left(A_t\right)^{h \ell}:=L |\phi^{\ell \to h}_t| .$$
    We have that  
    $$\Phi^N_t-{\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N_t\right]=\left(\frac{1}{N}\Theta A_t \Theta ^ \top \right) \circ \left(\Xi-{\mathbf E} \left[ \Xi\right]\right),$$
    where $\Theta_{ih}=\mathds 1 _{C(i)=h}$ for $i=1,\cdots,N$ and $h=1,\cdots,q$ and $\circ$ denotes the Hadamard (or component-wise) product.\\ Using Lemma 5.6.7 in \cite{HJ} we have that 
    $$\left \| \Phi^N_t-{\mathbf E} \left[\Phi^N_t\right] \right \|_2 \leq \frac{1}{N}\sqrt{\| I \circ \Theta A_tA_t^\top \Theta ^\top \|_2 \left \| I \circ \Theta \Theta ^\top \right \|_2} \left \| \Xi -{\mathbf E} \left[ \Xi\right]\right \|_2.$$
   A straightforward computation yields that $\left \| I \circ \Theta \Theta ^\top \right \|_2=1$ and $$\| I \circ \Theta A_tA_t^\top \Theta ^\top \|_2 \leq L^2\sum_{h,\ell=1}^q\left | \phi^{\ell \to h}_t\right |^2.$$ Since all norms are equivalent in ${\mathbb R}^{q \times q}$, we have that 
   $$\sqrt{\| I \circ \Theta A_tA_t^\top \Theta ^\top \|_2} \leq C \sum_{h,\ell =1}^q \left | \phi^{h \to \ell}_t\right |,$$
   for some constant $C$ that only depends on $q$. 
   We then conclude using Lemma \ref{lmm:vershynin}.
head: environment
